{"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Q is defined as the primes dividing A, but every later step (and the final L) requires Q = all primes ≤ A; a one-line but central definitional slip.", "errors": [{"description": "The set Q is defined as the primes dividing A, yet the Lemma's proof uses 'every prime in P(x)\σ(x) is greater than A' and 'if all prime factors of x are at most A then σ(x)=P(x)', which hold only for Q = {p prime, p ≤ A}. Read literally the Lemma (and hence L) is false; the write-up's own falsification item 1 refutes the divides-A version. Repairable typo, but internally contradictory.", "quote": "Q=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid A\},
\qquad
\sigma(x)=P(x)\cap Q."}, {"description": "The sentence justifying the definition repeats the wrong (and, per the author's own remark, false) principle that only primes dividing a_1 matter; sharing a factor with A only shows σ(x)≠∅, not that non-divisors of A are irrelevant.", "quote": "Only the primes dividing \(A\) can matter here, because every term shares a prime factor with \(A=a_1\)."}, {"description": "In the converse of (1) the existence of n with a_n < m < a_{n+1} tacitly requires m > a_1; this is true since m ≥ A and m is not a term, but is left unstated.", "quote": "By unboundedness there is an \(n\) with
\[
a_n<m<a_{n+1}.
\]"}], "notes": "Structure (scan characterization, small-prime erasure via m=Rp^k, global L-periodicity from threshold A, counting T) is correct and rigorous; the bounds m<x and the contradiction step all check out. Only the mis-stated definition of Q blocks a 7."}
